<a id="add-beam-annotations"></a>

### Add beam annotations

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-13 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** annotate each beam in this plan in one go: a beam tag at its start, middle or end and spot elevations on its top or bottom at its ends.

Revit's Annotate > Beam Annotations: on each beam handed in, in one plan, a beam tag at its start, middle or end, and spot elevations on its top (top of steel) or bottom at one or both ends, of the tag and spot types named or the project's defaults. Beams already tagged in that plan are left alone and named. Says per beam what it placed - the tag, each spot and the level it shows - and why it left anything else.

<a id="arrange-tags"></a>

### Arrange tags

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** the tags are sitting on top of each other, spread them out.

Pushes overlapping tags apart until nothing sits on top of anything else, leaving every tag as near where it started as it can be. The tidy-up for tags that ALREADY exist - placed by hand, or by an earlier run - which is the case a placement job cannot reach, because that only arranges the tags it places itself. **A TAG'S BOUNDING BOX INCLUDES ITS LEADER, SO IT CANNOT BE USED TO MEASURE THE TAG.** On a leadered tag the box wraps the head AND the leader line - on a congested plan that is metres, not millimetres, and spacing derived from it flings tags across the drawing. Sizes are therefore measured ONLY from leaderless tags, each spaced by its own, and the leadered ones take the median of their own tag type's. Where every tag in the set has a leader nothing can be measured at all, and the caller's stated size is used instead: a size somebody chose beats a measured number that is silently wrong. Which of the two happened is reported. **A BENT LEADER HAS ALREADY BEEN THREADED ROUND SOMETHING, SO IT STAYS PUT.** An elbow means somebody - or an earlier pass - routed that tag past a duct, another tag, or its own text. Nudging it reopens a problem that was already solved. When exactly one tag of a clashing pair has a straight leader, that one takes the whole separation; only a pair of the same kind splits it. Straight or bent is read fresh from each tag's current elbow, never remembered. **THAT PREFERENCE CAN FAIL TO CONVERGE, SO IT IS TWO PHASES.** A tag boxed in by bent-leader neighbours has nowhere to go alone. The first phase keeps the preference; anything still clashing at the end of it is separated with both tags moving, and the tags that needed the exception are named. A preference must not silently block a real clash, and must not be silently dropped either. **MOVING A TAG DRAGS A FREE LEADER'S END OFF ITS ELEMENT.** A leader whose end is attached follows the element it points at. A free one carries its own end point, which travels with the head - so a bulk tidy-up quietly pulls every arrow off the thing it was pointing at. Free ends are read before the move and written back after. **ROOM, SPACE AND AREA TAGS ARE ARRANGED TOO (version 2)**, by their head, so a door tag over a room tag is pushed apart. Asked to keep room tags still, they stay exactly where they are and the other tags move away from them. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="center-room-tags"></a>

### Center room tags

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** put the room tags back in the middle of their rooms.

Moves each room tag so its head sits at the middle of the room it tags. The tidy-up after tags have been dragged about, or after rooms were re-shaped and the tags stayed where they were. **THE MIDDLE OF AN L-SHAPED ROOM IS NOT INSIDE IT.** The true area centroid of an L or a U falls in the corridor, or in the next tenancy - and a tag placed there reads as belonging to the wrong room, which is worse than the untidy tag it replaced. So the centroid is TESTED against the room before it is used, and where it falls outside, a point that is genuinely inside is found by sampling. Every tag that needed that is named, because those are the rooms worth looking at on screen. **THE CENTROID IS AREA-WEIGHTED, NOT THE MIDDLE OF THE BOX.** A bounding-box centre is right for a rectangle and wrong for everything else, and it is wrong in the direction that puts the tag in a doorway. The polygon centroid is computed from the room's own boundary; the box is the fallback for a room whose boundary cannot be read at all. **A TAG ON A ROOM IN A LINKED MODEL NEEDS THE LINK'S TRANSFORM.** On an MEP job the rooms are usually in the architect's link. The room's centre then comes back in the LINK's coordinates, and using it directly puts the tag at the wrong end of the site - far enough away that it looks like a different bug. The link's transform is applied, and a tag whose link cannot be resolved is refused rather than moved to a guessed place. **THE HEAD IS WHAT MOVES.** Setting the tag's location does not move a room tag; its head position is the property that does. Every tag is read back after the move and reported at where it actually landed. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16), so a whole plan's worth of tags is one undo entry.

<a id="copy-tags-to-replacements"></a>

### Copy tags to replacements

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-22 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** give each replacement element the tags its old element carries, in every view.

When elements are replaced - in-place units by a loadable family, one family by another - makes on each new element a copy of every tag its old element carries, anywhere in the model: same view, same tag type, same head position, same leader on or off, end condition and orientation, and the leader end and elbow where Revit takes them. Any category; which old element goes to which new one is a file of id pairs. IT EXISTS BECAUSE NO RELEASE LETS A TAG BE POINTED AT ANOTHER ELEMENT. On 2026-10-12, on Revit 2020, three in-place split units were replaced by a loadable family and their 16 tags of "TCM_TG_HVAC Equipment: Equipment Tag", across 9 floor plans and sections, all with leaders, had to be re-made by hand. The only route is a new tag on the new element and the old tag's type put on it. **TAG_ELEMENTS WAS WEIGHED AND NOT WIDENED.** It places one type, chosen by the caller, at each element's own location in ONE view. This takes the view, the type, the head and the leader from each OLD TAG, across every view, and takes pairs rather than elements. Folding that in would give one card two jobs, and TAG_ELEMENTS was PROVEN then - a change under its impl/ would make its proof stale. It is retired now. **IT NEVER DELETES THE OLD TAGS.** Deleting the old element takes them with it, and that is the modeller's decision. Until then old and new tags sit side by side, so the drawing can be compared before anything is lost. **THE TYPE IS READ BACK.** IndependentTag.Create has made a tag of the default type instead of the one passed (FRG-VIEW-030), so it is checked and ChangeTypeId'd, and a tag that will not take the old type is removed again in the same undo. If the typed route throws, the tag is made by category (multi-category for a multi-category tag) and then changed. **EVERYTHING ELSE IS READ BACK TOO, AND WHAT DIFFERS IS NAMED PER VIEW.** An elbow on an ATTACHED leader may not hold - Revit owns that leader's shape - and the end is never freed to force it, because a free end stops following the element. The tag is kept and the elbow named. **IT REFUSES, AND SAYS SO,** a tag pointing at several elements (2022 on), a material tag, a view where the new element is not seen, and a new id not among the elements handed in. An old element with no tag anywhere makes nothing and is named. A second run finds every tag already there and makes none. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-angular-dimension"></a>

### Create angular dimension

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-03 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** dimension the angle between two grids, planes, lines or wall faces, in a plan.

Draws an angular dimension between two references, along an arc. **THE LIBRARY HAD NO ANGLE AT ALL.** Every dimension fragment here measures a DISTANCE - duct spacing, grids, rooms, wall openings, family instances. A splayed wall, a skewed grid and a bend in a run are all dimensioned by angle on a real drawing and nothing could draw one. **THE CALL IS `AngularDimension.Create`, NOT `NewAngularDimension`.** The obvious-sounding one is on the FAMILY EDITOR's creation object and cannot be reached from a project at all. This one is a static on the DB type and works in a project on every release - which is the opposite of the radial case, where no project route exists before 2025. **THE ARC IS WHERE THE DIMENSION SITS, NOT WHAT IT MEASURES.** It is the witness line's path, and its centre must be the apex of the angle. An arc struck somewhere convenient gives a dimension that reads a different angle from the one intended, with no error. **VERSION 2 TAKES WHAT CAN BE TYPED, AND STRIKES THE ARC ITSELF (2026-10-03).** Version 1 asked for a Revit `Arc` and `Reference` objects, which no request can carry - FRAGMENT-ISSUES section 6 and D-72. Now the two arms are named, `|` between them - `grid A`, `plane Skew`, `line <id>`, `wall <id> exterior` or `interior` - and the arc is made here, centred where the arms meet in plan, so its centre IS the apex. Only the radius is asked for. It spans the angle under 180 degrees between the arms' far ends. Plans only: that is where the arms meet. **READ BACK.** `measured` is the angle Revit reads off the dimension, in degrees. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-dimension"></a>

### Create dimension

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** put one dimension string through these on this view - parallel runs or fixtures.

Draws one linear dimension across a set of parallel linear elements in a view, measuring centre to centre - or through family instances. **This is the duct-spacing dimension.** It dimensions between the CENTRELINES of linear elements - ducts, pipes, conduit, cable tray - which is how MEP spacing is dimensioned and checked. It does not dimension to wall faces, grids or levels, or between two points the user names. Those are real jobs and each needs a different kind of reference. **A reference has to be asked for before it exists.** Revit only hands back referenceable geometry when the geometry is read with `ComputeReferences` turned on, and an MEP centreline additionally only appears when non-visible objects are included. Read the geometry the ordinary way and every element yields nothing, with no error - the dimension simply never gets made. **AN AXIS MAY BE NAMED, AND IT READS BACK** (version 2, when DIMENSION_MEP_RUNS was merged in). Left empty, the string is measured across the runs at whatever angle they sit. `x` or `y` measures along that axis of the model - the way to dimension between risers, vertical pipes seen end-on in a plan, which have no direction across them on the view. The dimension Revit made is read back: `dimensionedCount` is the references it holds, and fewer than two will not survive a commit. `problem` says in one sentence why nothing was drawn. This is version 2; version 1's proof no longer describes the code and is kept as a record, and the fragment is DRAFT until it is proved again. **VERSION 3 DIMENSIONS FAMILY INSTANCES TOO** (DIMENSION_FAMILY_INSTANCES merged in). An air terminal, fixture or piece of equipment has no centreline; its built-in centre references are used instead, along the axis named - x or y, which it needs. One that publishes none is named in `noReference`. Runs and instances handed in together are refused, nothing drawn: one string is one kind. **IT CANNOT DIMENSION A ROOM** - a room's boundary offers none of these references - and says so. | What you are dimensioning | Use | |---|---| | Ducts, pipes, conduit, cable tray | **this fragment** - their centrelines | | Grids, or levels in a section or elevation | `CREATE_LINEAR_DIMENSION` - "grid A, grid B" | | Air terminals, fixtures, equipment - any family instance | **this fragment**, axis x or y - built-in centre references, which a run does not have | | Rooms - "dimension the rooms", "put the room sizes on the plan" | `DIMENSION_ROOMS`; to know them, `REPORT_ROOM_SPACE_DATA` |

<a id="create-linear-dimension"></a>

### Create linear dimension

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** dimension between these grids, levels, planes, lines or wall faces, on this view - for builders work too.

Draws one linear dimension along a line, between the references given. **THE PLAIN DIMENSION, WHICH THE LIBRARY DID NOT HAVE.** `CREATE_DIMENSION` reads as the general one and is not: its own purpose calls it *"the duct-spacing dimension, and that is the whole of its scope"* - centre to centre, across parallel linear elements. Every other dimension fragment is similarly specific - grids and levels, rooms, wall openings, family instances, MEP runs. Measured 2026-09-18, none of them answers *"dimension from this to that"*. **THE REFERENCES ARE THE CALLER'S AND ARE NOT GUESSED.** A face, an edge, a centreline and a grid are four different references on the same wall, and which one a drawing should dimension to is a drafting decision, not something to infer (D-33). Working them out is the composing skill's job; this draws the dimension. **TWO REFERENCES IS THE MINIMUM AND MORE IS A STRING.** Three or more on one line gives the chained dimension a drawing actually carries, which is why the input is a list rather than a pair. **VERSION 2 TAKES WHAT CAN BE TYPED (2026-10-03).** Version 1 asked for Revit `Reference` objects and a `Line`, which no request can carry, so nothing could run it - FRAGMENT-ISSUES section 6 and D-72. It now takes, `|` between them: `grid A`, `level Level 2`, `plane Box Left`, `line <id>` (a model or detail line) and `wall <id> exterior` or `interior` - an id as Revit shows it, or a unique id. A face picked with the mouse still cannot be said and is not offered. The line the string sits on is two points in millimetres. **READ BACK.** The dimension's references are counted and each segment's value is read again, so `measured` is what Revit measured, not what was asked. **VERSION 5 IS THE ONE TOOL FOR GRIDS AND LEVELS.** A grid or level this view does not show, an arc grid, or a grid with a level is refused, nothing drawn. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-radial-dimension"></a>

### Create radial dimension

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** dimension the radius or diameter of an arc grid or an arc line, on this view.

Draws a radial or a diameter dimension on an arc. **IT IS REVIT 2025 AND LATER, AND THAT IS THE API'S LIMIT RATHER THAN A CHOICE MADE HERE.** Measured 2026-09-18 against every reference assembly 2020 to 2027: `RadialDimension.Create` first appears at 2025. Before that the only radial call in the whole API is `NewRadialDimension`, which belongs to the FAMILY EDITOR and cannot be reached from a project document. So on Revit 2020 to 2024 a radius simply cannot be dimensioned through the API, by this library or any other. **RADIUS AND DIAMETER ARE ONE CALL WITH A FLAG.** `isDiameter` is the whole difference, which is why this is one fragment and not two. **A DIAMETER DIMENSION IS STILL NOT AVAILABLE ANYWHERE ELSE.** `DiameterDimension.Create` does not exist on any release - checked at all eight. This flag is the only project route to one, and it too starts at 2025. **THE REFERENCE MUST BE AN ARC, AND ITS ORIGIN MUST LIE WITHIN THE ARC.** Revit says so itself and throws otherwise; the message is caught and repeated in words rather than surfaced as an exception. **VERSION 2 TAKES WHAT CAN BE TYPED (2026-10-03).** Version 1 asked for a Revit `Reference`, which no request can carry - FRAGMENT-ISSUES section 6 and D-72 - so it could be run by nobody. Now the arc is `grid NAME` for an arc grid or `line <id>` for an arc model or detail line. An arc edge of a solid still has to be picked with the mouse and is not offered. **READ BACK.** `measured` is what the dimension reads, and it must equal the arc's own radius or diameter to half a millimetre or the call fails. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="dimension-rooms"></a>

### Dimension rooms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-10 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** put the room sizes on the plan as real dimensions.

Draws real Revit dimensions across each room - its overall width and depth, wall face to wall face - just outside the room. Live dimension elements that update with the model, not text that goes stale the moment a wall moves. **THREE DIFFERENT NUMBERS COME OFF THE SAME ROOM AND ALL THREE ARE ASKED FOR.** Inside is the clear room size, the number a client means by *"how big is the room"* and the one that agrees with the room's area. Outside is face to outer face, what an envelope or a plot line is checked against. Centre is wall centreline to centreline, the setting-out size that agrees with the grid. On a room 8800 clear between 200 walls those are 8800, 9200 and 9000 - three right answers to three different questions, so `measureTo` is a request input and has no default worth trusting. **THE FACE IS PICKED BY DISTANCE, NEVER BY ITS NAME.** Revit offers a wall's faces as interior and exterior LAYERS, and which of those bounds the room depends on which way the wall was drawn - so choosing by name gets it right about half the time, silently. The nearest face to the room boundary is the one bounding it and the farthest is the outer one, whatever they are called. **EVERY DIMENSION IS READ BACK AND CHECKED AGAINST A NUMBER WORKED OUT A DIFFERENT WAY.** The expected size comes from the room's own boundary extent plus each wall's real thickness, and the dimension's own value is read after it is created. A disagreement is reported per room rather than left on the drawing: the usual cause is a wall type whose location line is not its centre, which makes the centre mode quietly measure to a face. **AN L-SHAPED ROOM GETS ITS OVERALL SIZE, WHICH MAY NOT BE WHAT IS WANTED.** Width and depth of the whole extent is one honest answer for a concave room and it is not the same as dimensioning each leg. Rooms that are not rectangular are dimensioned and named, so they can be looked at. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="force-tag-leader-lshape"></a>

### Force tag leader lshape

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** make the tag leaders bend into the tag instead of running diagonally.

Bends every tag's leader into an L - a short horizontal leg into the tag, then a straight run to the element - instead of one diagonal line. The drafting standard on most issued drawings, applied in bulk. **THE ELBOW WILL NOT TAKE UNTIL THE LEADER END IS FREE.** With the end attached, Revit owns the leader's shape and setting an elbow is quietly ignored - the call returns, nothing bends, and the tag looks untouched. The end condition is set first, which is a real change to how that leader behaves: a free end no longer follows its element when the element moves. That trade is the whole reason this is a deliberate act rather than a setting. **AND A ROOM TAG HAS NO END CONDITION TO SET.** The property is not on that class at all, on any release - the compile gate caught it the first time this was written to mirror the independent-tag branch. Its elbow is set directly and read back, which is what says whether it took. **TAG CLASSES SHARE NO BASE THAT CARRIES A LEADER.** An independent tag and a room, space or area tag each declare their own elbow, end and head. Casting to the independent kind alone silently skips every room tag in the set and reports the rest as done, so both are handled explicitly - which the compiler checks, and a name lookup does not. **THE LEG IS A PAPER LENGTH.** How long the horizontal shoulder should be is judged on the printed sheet, so the number is multiplied by the view scale. A model-distance leg is invisible at 1:200 and absurd at 1:20. **THE LEG POINTS TOWARD THE ELEMENT.** A shoulder that leaves the tag on the wrong side crosses back over the text, which is worse than the diagonal it replaced. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="move-annotation"></a>

### Move annotation

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** put this tag exactly here, rather than wherever a rule decides.

Moves an annotation - a tag, a dimension, a text note - to a point the caller names, or lines a set of them up or spaces them evenly in their view (version 2). **NOTHING IN THE LIBRARY MOVED AN ANNOTATION TO A POINT, AND THAT IS A SHAPE RATHER THAN ONE MISSING FRAGMENT.** Every tag fragment here is RULE-based: `ARRANGE_TAGS` spreads them out, `STACK_TAGS` columns them at the side or parks them down the edges, `CENTER_ROOM_TAGS` puts them back in the middle. All of them decide the position themselves. Not one takes a position. So *move this tag*, *move this dimension* and *set the tag location* were one missing capability wearing three names. **A TAG IS MOVED BY ITS HEAD, NOT BY ITS LOCATION.** `IndependentTag` carries `TagHeadPosition`, and moving the element instead drags the whole tag including its leader anchor. Those are different results and only one of them is what somebody asking to move a tag means. **THE LEADER IS NOT TOUCHED.** What the tag points AT stays what it points at; only where the head sits changes. A fragment that re-anchored the leader while moving the head would quietly re-tag things. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="offset-tags-from-host"></a>

### Offset tags from host

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** move each tag a set distance off its own element, with or without a leader, and turn each tag horizontal, vertical or to the orientation of its element.

Moves every tag handed in to the same offset from ITS OWN element - so many paper millimetres right and up - switches its leader on, off, or leaves it, and turns the tag Horizontal, Vertical, Model, or the way its own element runs, or leaves it turned as it is. Any tag: air terminal, duct, pipe, equipment, door, window and opening tags, and room, space and area tags. Which tags, how far, the leader and the orientation are all values; nothing here knows about diffusers or openings. IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE TAGS ON A 1:75 AIR TERMINAL PLAN SAT ON TOP OF THEIR DIFFUSERS after the tag family was edited, and every tag fragment in the library decides the position by its own rule. `ARRANGE_TAGS` pushes clashing tags apart, `STACK_TAGS` columns them at one point, `MOVE_ANNOTATION` puts them all at ONE point, `CENTER_ROOM_TAGS` puts room tags in the middle of their rooms, `FORCE_TAG_LEADER_LSHAPE` bends leaders. None takes "8 mm right and 6 mm up of each tag's own element". Widening was weighed and refused: ARRANGE and STACK are PROVEN, so their proofs would go stale, and each is a different rule; MOVE_ANNOTATION's contract is one target for every element, and a second mode there would give one card two jobs. **MEASURED FROM THE ELEMENT, NEVER FROM THE HEAD.** The target is the element's location plus the offset, so a second run finds every tag already there and moves nothing. That second run is also the read-back. The location is the element's point - an air terminal, a door, equipment, a room - or the middle of its line - a duct, a pipe. Anything with neither is measured from the centre of its box and COUNTED, because a box centre is a guess. **THE OFFSET IS ON PAPER, IN THE VIEW'S OWN PLANE.** 8 mm right on the sheet is 600 mm in the model at 1:75, and "right" is the view's right, which is not the model's X on a rotated plan. The head keeps its own depth, so a diffuser 2.7 m up does not pull its tag off the view. **"LEADER ON" MEANS ON AND ATTACHED.** A free end stays where it was put when the element moves, which is not a leader to the element. A room, space or area tag has no end condition on any release, so for those the leader is switched on and its end stays where the tag is anchored in the room. With the leader left as it is, a free end is put back after the move rather than dragged along with the head. **A TAG THAT POINTS AT SEVERAL ELEMENTS (2022 on) IS LEFT ALONE AND NAMED.** Which of them it should sit beside is not answerable here. **THE SHEET STAYS WHERE IT WAS PUT.** Changing tags in a placed view has moved its viewport on the sheet - 30 and 43 mm on 2026-09-27, with the box the same size. Each viewport of the view is read before, read again after a regenerate, and put back inside the same undo if it moved more than half a millimetre WITH ITS BOX THE SAME SIZE; the report gives both positions in paper millimetres. A box that changed size is reported and NOT put back: when tags past the plan's edge make it grow, its centre moves while the plan inside it does not, and recentring would shift the plan. **A REFUSED TAG IS LEFT AS IT WAS.** Revit refusing the move, or accepting it and reading the head back more than half a paper millimetre away, both put the tag's head, leader and end condition back. A kept free leader end is read back after the move, and one that travelled with the head is named in leaderNotAsAsked. **EVERYTHING HANDED IN IS ACCOUNTED FOR.** Tags of a category not asked for, tags in another view and things that are not tags are left alone and counted, never skipped silently. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="place-detail-components"></a>

### Place detail components

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-12 (Revit 2020, 2024).

**What it does:** put a detail component or an annotation symbol on this view at these points, in a project or in a family's own view.

Places a detail component - a detail item family - or an annotation symbol - a generic annotation such as a north arrow or a fire-rating symbol - on one view, once at each point given, turned if an angle is given. **THESE FAMILIES BELONG TO A VIEW, NOT TO A LEVEL.** PLACE_FAMILY_INSTANCES places model families on a level and cannot place one of these at all; a detail item or a symbol exists only in the view it was drawn in. So the view is asked for, and a family that is NOT view-based is refused by name and pointed at PLACE_FAMILY_INSTANCES. **IN A FAMILY TOO** (version 2, 2026-11-11). With a family open in the Family Editor, a detail item or a generic annotation LOADED INTO THE FAMILY - a diffuser's flow arrows - is placed in one of the family's own views, as Detail Component and Symbol do by hand: in the Ref. Level plan it shows in a project's plans only. The points are millimetres from the family's origin. The first one's id comes back as `instanceId`, for LOCK_NESTED_FAMILY_TO_PLANES to lock it to the family's planes and ARRAY_FAMILY_FORMS to array it. **READ BACK, ALL OR NOTHING** (version 2): each one placed is read again - it exists, its Owner View is the view asked for, its insertion point is where asked (half a millimetre, in the view's plane) and its type is the one asked. One that does not read so fails the call; nothing is kept. **A 3D VIEW OR A TEMPLATE IS REFUSED.** Revit draws neither kind in a 3D view, and a view template holds no elements. **The points are on the view's own plane, in millimetres.** On a plan that is X and Y; a drafting view is the same. **MEASURED 2026-11-12, REVIT 2020 (row 5b-1573):** inside a family, Revit reports a nested Detail Items family WorkPlaneBased and refuses it in a view ("its FamilyPlacementType is not ViewBased"), though the same file places as one in a project. So in a family only a type Revit reports ViewBased there is placed here; any other is refused up front with what Revit reports and the route that works: PLACE_FAMILY_INSTANCES on the level, then LOCK_NESTED_FAMILY_TO_PLANES, which locks it in the plan of its level. A family of category Detail Items or Generic Annotations counts as view-based in a project whatever placement type Revit reports. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION (Golden Rule 16). One operation is one undo entry, and the caller owns it.

<a id="place-flow-arrows"></a>

### Place flow arrows

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** show which way the air is going on the drawing.

Places flow-direction arrows along MEP runs in one view, at a spacing, pointing the way the air or water actually goes. **THE DIRECTION COMES FROM THE CONNECTORS, NOT FROM THE LINE.** A duct's location curve runs whichever way it happened to be drawn: start to end says nothing about flow. The connectors know - one is an inlet and one an outlet - and the arrow points from the first toward the second. Drawing along the curve instead puts half the arrows on a drawing backwards, with nothing to warn anybody, and a backwards arrow on an issued drawing is read as fact. **A RUN WHOSE CONNECTORS DO NOT SAY IS LEFT ALONE.** Plenty of ductwork is modelled without a system, and its connectors carry no direction at all. Those runs are named, not given an arrow chosen by the geometry - a guessed arrow is indistinguishable from a known one once it is on the sheet. **RISERS GET NOTHING, ON PURPOSE.** A vertical run seen in a plan has no meaningful arrow: the flow is towards or away from the reader. Near-vertical runs are counted and skipped rather than given a nonsense direction. **THE ARROWS ARE ANNOTATION AND LIVE IN ONE VIEW.** They do not appear in any other view, which is correct and is what somebody notices as absence. Place them per view being issued. **THE SYMBOL MUST ALREADY BE IN THE PROJECT AND MUST BE ACTIVATED.** This loads nothing - the arrow family is a drawing-office standard, not something to invent - and an inactive symbol makes the first placement throw, which is the classic first-use-in-a-session failure. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **view** - a view, by name - resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused<br>**arrow family name** - text<br>**arrow type name** - text<br>**spacing mm** - a number - digits only - 250 or 250.5, not 250mm |
| **You get** | placed |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `PLACE_FLOW_ARROWS` |

<a id="report-tags-and-targets"></a>

### Report tags and targets

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what is each tag on this drawing actually pointing at.

Every tag in a view and what it is really pointing at - including targets that live inside a LINKED model, and tags pointing at nothing at all. The check before a drawing is issued. Read-only. **HALF THE TAGS ON A COORDINATION DRAWING ARE INVISIBLE TO THE OBVIOUS CALL.** The accessor that returns local targets returns them only: on an MEP job the architecture is a link, so room tags, door tags and anything tagged on the architect's model come back as an EMPTY set - not an error, just nothing. A report built on it says the sheet has no tags on exactly the elements a coordination sheet exists to annotate. The link-aware accessor carries both halves of the answer: which link, and which element inside it. **AN ORPHANED TAG IS THE ONE THAT REACHES THE PRINTER.** A tag whose target was deleted, or whose link was unloaded, still draws - usually as a bare leader or a question mark. It is noticed on the printed sheet rather than on screen, which is the most expensive place to notice anything. Those are named separately from tags that point somewhere. **A TAG CAN POINT AT SEVERAL ELEMENTS SINCE 2022, AND TAKING THE FIRST IS WRONG.** A multi-reference tag genuinely annotates all of them. Every target is listed, and the tags carrying more than one are named, because they behave differently when anything is moved or deleted. It reports what the tags point at, not whether the text is right: a tag whose displayed value disagrees with the element's parameter is a different check. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **view** - a view, by name - resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused |
| **You get** | tag targets, linked tags, orphan tags, multi tags |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |

<a id="stack-tags"></a>

### Stack tags

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** stack these tags in a tidy column at the side, or park them in columns down both edges of the view.

Arranges tags into a neat vertical column at one point, each still leadered back to its own element. What a drafter does by hand beside a busy area, when there is no room for the tags where the elements are. **THE STACK ORDER IS NEAREST-ELEMENT-FIRST, NOT THE ORDER THE SET ARRIVED IN.** Tags are sorted by where their own element sits along the stack, so the leaders fan out without crossing. Stacking them in the order a filter happened to return produces a plate of spaghetti that looks like the tool is broken - and it is the same tags, in the same places, with the same leaders. **THE GAP IS A PAPER DISTANCE AND HAS TO BE MULTIPLIED BY THE VIEW SCALE.** Every millimetre in tag work is a paper millimetre: 5 mm between tags is 500 model mm at 1:100 and 250 at 1:50. Using the number as a model distance is the commonest mistake in this whole subject, and it produces a stack that is either unreadable or off the sheet. **IT MOVES HEADS AND LEAVES THE LEADERS TO FOLLOW.** An attached leader end stays on its element; a free one is carried back to where it was, so the arrows do not come off the things they point at. **Or two columns down the view's edges** (version 2, from ARRANGE_TAGS_TO_VIEW_EDGES) - the "I cannot read the drawing for tags" fix on a busy services plan. Each tag goes to the side its own element is on, so the leaders stay short; each column follows the elements up the view, so they do not cross; the margin is paper millimetres from the crop, or from the tags' own extent when the view is not cropped, and the answer says which. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **view** - a view, by name - resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused<br>**stack at** - a point - MILLIMETRES, "x,y,z"; optional, left out means *0,0,0*<br>**gap mm** - a number - digits only - 250 or 250.5, not 250mm<br>**layout** - text; optional, left out means *point*<br>**margin mm** - text; optional, left out means *none* |
| **You get** | stacked, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
3. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
4. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"tag all the areas in this area plan"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
5. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"put area tags on these areas"*

<a id="tag-material-or-multi-category"></a>

### Tag material or multi category

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-13 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** material tags or multi-category tags, of the material or multi-category tag type named - Revit's Material Tag and Multi-Category Tag.

Revit's Annotate > Material Tag and Multi-Category Tag: one material tag, or one multi-category tag, on each one handed in, of the material or multi-category tag type the modeller names - the type decides which. One already carrying that kind of tag there is left and named, and so is every other one it does not tag, with why.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **view** - a view, by name - resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused<br>**tag type** - text; optional, left out means *none*<br>**add leader** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | tagged, new tags, mismatched, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `TAG_MATERIAL_OR_MULTI_CATEGORY` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
3. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
4. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"add material tags to these walls"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
5. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"tag the materials of this floor"* · *"multi-category tag these elements"*

<a id="tag-views-by-rules"></a>

### Tag views by rules

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-16 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** put tags on every element of the named categories in several views at once, by a rule per category - tag type, leader, shortest run - setting each new tag apart from the others.

Places new tags in one view or many in a single pass, following a rule per category - which tag type, whether a straight leader may be drawn, the shortest run worth a tag - and sets each new tag down apart from the others already placed, trying spots around its element before drawing it out on a leader. Elements already tagged are left alone, and every view is one undo. Says per view what it placed, what was crowded, and why anything was left.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **views** - comma separated, resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused; optional<br>**rules** - text<br>**min gap mm** - a number - digits only - 250 or 250.5, not 250mm; optional, left out means *2*<br>**skip tagged** - yes or no - true or false; optional, left out means *true* |
| **You get** | tagged, new tags, leaders drawn, type corrections, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `TAG_VIEWS_BY_RULES` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"annotation template and tag in one pass, no overlaps"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"batch tag over many views"*
